articles.title: Rybakina estrena su condición de nº1 con una derrota ante la número 118 y se tomará una semana de descanso
articles.standfirst: Alina Charaeva protagoniza la sorpresa del WTA de Pekín y la kazaja anuncia que "es momento de descansar" para recuperarse del pie izquierdo
articles.summary: Alina Charaeva protagoniza la sorpresa del WTA de Pekín y la kazaja anuncia que "es momento de descansar" para recuperarse del pie izquierdo
articles.body: Ha saltado la sorpresa en el 'National Tennis Center' de Pekín. Elena Rybakina, que estrenaba su condición como reina del circuito femenino desde que firmara su pase a las semifinales del US Open, ha caído derrotada a manos de la armenia Alina Charaeva (118 del mundo) por 3-6, 6-4 y 6-3 en la segunda ronda del WTA 1000 asiático. Desde 1975, la nacida en Samara se ha convertido en la jugadora de menor ranking en remontar a una número 1. En dos horas y 12 minutos el público de la 'Diamond Court' se ha quedado sin la máxima favorita al título. La joven de 24 años le dio la vuelta al set y 'break' de la kazaja. La seguridad al primer servicio de Alina fue lo que la impulsó. Ganó el 76% de los puntos que disputó con este. La derrota puso fin a una racha de catorce victorias consecutivas de Rybakina en sus estrenos en torneos WTA 1000. La armenia buscará prolongar su semana mágica en la capital china ante la británica Sonay Kartal (129). Tras caer eliminada, la campeona del grande neoyorquino anunció unos días de descanso para poder recuperarse de las molestias que sufre en el pie izquierdo, y que la obligaron a jugar bajo los efectos de analgésicos en las pistas de Flushing Meadows: "Noté un poco el pie al final del partido, así que es momento de descansar un poco y ver qué viene en las próximas semanas", señalaba. "Pasaron muchas cosas después de la victoria en el Abierto de Estados Unidos. No tuve muchas oportunidades de dormir y recuperarme", afirmó Rybakina, pagando el cansancio de una temporada larga. Tampoco pudo ayudar a su país en las finales de la Billie Jean King Cup. No ha querido precisar próximas citas, aunque figura apuntada en el WTA 1000 de Wuhan (12 al 18 de octubre), segundo torneo de la categoría en la gira asiática femenina.

articles.title: John McEnroe names the American man he thinks has the best chance of winning a Grand Slam title
articles.summary: John McEnroe loves American tennis and has maintained that mindset even well into his retirement. As a player, he never missed a Davis Cup match,...
articles.body:
John McEnroe loves American tennis and has maintained that mindset even well into his retirement.

As a player, he never missed a Davis Cup match, referencing some of those triumphs among the best of his entire storied career.

Then, once he stopped playing, the 67-year-old took up the mantle of Davis Cup captain, resigning after just 14 months, as he failed to get regular commitments from the stars of the era like Pete Sampras and Andre Agassi.

Now a prominent and outspoken pundit, he continues to fly the flag proudly when given the opportunity.

Speaking as a Eurosport and TNT Sports pundit recently, John McEnroe has now named the American man he thinks is the closest to claiming a Grand Slam title.

John McEnroe previews the future of men's tennis in America

It has been 23 long years since we last saw a US man lift a major, although we came close just last month when Ben Shelton reached the US Open final.

Sadly, he failed to challenge Alexander Zverev, but it marked a huge breakthrough for the 23-year-old.

This likely prompted McEnroe's choice, as he noted: "People ask me all the time when we are going to get an American winning a Grand Slam and I put Ben (Shelton) at the top of the list.

"We wait to see what happens with players like (Jakub) Mensik or [Joao] Fonseca and whether these young kids can get over the hump and challenge Sinner and Alcaraz.

"Or will Sascha Zverev be dominant and win a few more Grand Slams over the next few years?

"Carlos and Jannik were a long way ahead of the rest for the last couple of years and injuries have stopped that this year, so it's an interesting question moving forward who will step up."

Then, discussing the wider topic of American tennis, he feared for participation, with other sports seemingly taking precedent and thus hoovering up the elite athletes.

McEnroe added: "It feels to me that tennis is more accessible in other countries, especially Europe.

"In our country, to be blunt, the accessibility is a big issue. The best athletes play American football, basketball, in some cases, soccer. You have the affordability issues and tennis is expensive."

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: India’s biggest hits and flops - from historic golf gold to tennis medal drought
articles.summary: India signed off from the Asian Games 2026 in fourth place with 85 medals — 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.
articles.body: India signed off from the Asian Games 2026 in fourth place with 85 medals — 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze. The final tally was below the record 106 medals won at Hangzhou, but a strong finish in the final days changed the complexion of the campaign.From Kumkum Mohod’s historic archery gold and Aman Sehrawat’s wrestling triumph to disappointing campaigns in tennis and some traditionally strong disciplines, India’s Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games journey had its share of soaring highs and hard misses.Here are India's biggest hits and flops from Aichi-Nagoya.The Hits1. Archery: The biggest gold-medal successArchery was arguably India's biggest success story when it came to gold medals.India won five gold medals, with the women's and men's compound teams, mixed compound team, women's recurve team and Kumkum Mohod's individual recurve triumph providing the highlights.The biggest moment came from 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod, who became the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve gold at the Asian Games.Her success, along with the women's recurve team's gold, gave Indian archery a memorable Games. Kumkum also added a silver in the mixed recurve team event with Dhiraj Bommadevara.2. Hockey: Two golds and Olympic qualificationIndian hockey delivered when it mattered most.The women's team ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games gold, while Harmanpreet Singh's men's team defeated Malaysia 5-1 in the final to retain the title.The two victories also had an Olympic dimension, with India's performances securing qualification opportunities for Los Angeles 2028.The men's final was the perfect way to close India's medal campaign, with the 5-1 victory delivering the country's 21st gold.3. Cricket: Both teams defend their titlesIndia's cricket teams delivered two more gold medals.The women's team retained its title, while the men's side defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the final to successfully defend India's Asian Games crown. Abhishek Sharma's explosive batting and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51 were among the highlights of the men's final.The men's final also became one of the most talked-about sporting moments of the Games, thanks to the India-Pakistan rivalry.4. Boxing: Three goldsIndia's boxers produced one of the strongest late surges of the Games, winning three gold medals.Lovlina Borgohain, Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal emerged as champions in their respective categories.For Lovlina, the victory was particularly significant: she became only the second Indian woman after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games boxing gold.5. Wrestling: Aman Sehrawat's comebackAman Sehrawat's gold was one of the more compelling individual stories of the Games.The wrestler had endured a difficult period involving illness, absences and a loss of motivation following the Paris Olympics. His return to the top at Aichi-Nagoya turned the campaign into a personal comeback story as well as a medal-winning one.India finished with two wrestling golds, along with silver and bronze medals.6. Pranavi Urs makes golf historyPranavi Urs created history by winning India's first women's individual golf gold at the Asian Games.India also took silver in the women's team event, making golf one of the country's notable success stories in Aichi-Nagoya.7. Kabaddi: India keep its Asian Games dominanceKabaddi remained one of India's most dependable gold-medal sports at Aichi-Nagoya.Both the men's and women's teams won gold, allowing India to retain its titles and reinforce its dominance in the sport at the Asian Games.The double triumph was another strong performance from a discipline where India continues to set the continental benchmark.8. Athletics: India's biggest medal contributorAthletics was India's biggest contributor by overall medal count, producing 24 medals.The medal haul included silver medals for Ancy Sojan, Sarvesh Kushare, Sawan Berwal, Gulveer Singh and others, along with multiple bronze medals across track and field.The sport also produced historic moments, including Baranica Elangovan's first-ever Asian Games pole-vault medal for India and Vithya Ramraj's national-record bronze in the 400m hurdles.The caveat is the gold count. Athletics produced a huge volume of medals but only one gold, meaning the sport's conversion into top-of-the-podium finishes remains an area India will want to improve.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyThe Flops1. Tennis: A historic medal droughtTennis was arguably India's biggest disappointment.For the first time in four decades, India failed to win a single Asian Games tennis medal. The campaign ended without a podium finish despite the country's historically strong record in the sport at the continental event.The result was particularly striking because tennis has traditionally been one of India's reliable Asian Games medal sports.2. Shooting: Too many near misses before the turnaroundShooting eventually contributed 15 medals, including three golds, making it one of India's biggest medal-producing sports.But the campaign began with considerable disappointment.India endured several fourth-place finishes and missed opportunities before Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet finally ended the wait for a shooting gold.Tilottama Sen and Vidarsa Vinod, for example, finished fourth and fifth respectively in the women's 50m rifle 3P individual final.The final medal count was impressive, but expectations around India's shooters were even higher.3. Badminton: Below expectationsBadminton managed only one medal — a bronze in the men's team event.The result was underwhelming for a sport that has produced some of India's biggest Asian Games and Olympic stars.The campaign was also overshadowed by criticism of the Games' scheduling and organisation. H.S. Prannoy, who won the men's team bronze, described the experience as “sad” for athletes and criticised the accommodation and scheduling arrangements.4. Equestrian: A quiet disappointmentEquestrian was another discipline that failed to make a mark for India at Aichi-Nagoya.Despite India's pedigree in the sport and its strong performances at previous Asian Games, the contingent returned without a medal.The result added to a list of disciplines where India was unable to convert participation and experience into podium finishes, making equestrian a relatively disappointing campaign.5. Table tennis, fencing, esports, rowing all disappointSeveral disciplines failed to make a significant impact for India at the Asian Games 2026. Esports was among the clearest disappointments, with India failing to win a medal across its events, while fencing and volleyball also ended without a podium finish despite sizeable contingents and expectations.Table tennis managed only one bronze, a modest return for a sport with India’s growing international stature, making it another underwhelming campaign.Rowing produced a solitary bronze, leaving the discipline with a relatively limited medal haul. Taken together, these results highlight the gaps India still needs to address beyond its stronger medal-producing sports.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El 'qualy' Munar se cuela en Tokio en su octava semifinal del circuito
articles.standfirst: El mallorquín cede sólo seis juegos en los cuartos con el francés Jacquet
articles.summary: El mallorquín cede sólo seis juegos en los cuartos con el francés Jacquet
articles.body: El tenis masculino español ya tiene a un representante en las semifinales del Open 500 de Tokio. Se trata de Jaume Munar, que ha dado buena cuenta este domingo de Kyryan Jacquet, por 6-4 y 6-2, en apenas 1 hora y 40 minutos. Munar, el 64 del ranking y procedente de la previa, se cuela en la primera semifinal de la presente temporada y la octava de su carrera. Es el sexto jugador que llega tan lejos en el certamen como 'qualy'. Para encontrar la última vez que estuvo entre los cuatro mejores de un torneo del circuito había que remontarse a Basilea 2025. El mallorquín, de 29 años, espera en la penúltima ronda del lunes al ganador del cruce de cuartos entre su compatriota Carlos Alcaraz y Denis Shapovalov. La victoria del murciano aseguraría la presencia de un miembro de la Armada' en la final. Munar acumula ya cinco partidos ganados en la capital japonesa. Desde la fase clasificatoria, ha dejado por el camino a nombres como Taylor Fritz, que era el tercer cabeza de serie del certamen. Jaume ha ascendido ya 15 posiciones en las listas. Es virtualmente el número 49. Su temporada ha estado marcada por la lesión en el brazo en los cuartos de Rotterdam ante Alexander Bublik que le privó de estar después en Doha, Dubái, y los tres primeros Masters 1000 del calendario: Indian Wells, Miami y Montecarlo.

articles.title: Alcaraz pasa otra ronda por la retirada de Shapovalov y asegura un español en la final de Tokio
articles.standfirst: El murciano, verdugo del canadiense, se las verá este lunes con su compatriota Munar
articles.summary: El murciano, verdugo del canadiense, se las verá este lunes con su compatriota Munar
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz lo ha vuelto a hacer. Por tercer día consecutivo, ha firmado una remontada en Tokio para encadenar presencias en las semifinales, igualando a Rafael Nadal. Este lo hizo en 2010 y 2011. Alcaraz, primer favorito del certamen, ha acabado este domingo con la dura resistencia de Denis Shapovalov, por 7-6(3), 2-1 y retirada del canadiense por lesión. El vencedor se acordó del adversario en su firma a la cámara: "Regresa pronto Denis". Un gesto que le engrandece aún más. El duelo fratricida en la semifinal con Jaume Munar asegura la presencia de un español en la final por séptima vez desde 1972. Además de Alcaraz, vigente campeón, se plantaron en la lucha por el título Manolo Orantes (1975 y 1977); David Ferrer (2007) y Nadal (2010-11). "Es todo de cabeza, vas a ir a más", le decía su entrenador Samuel López desde el banquillo. Carlitos parecía haber hecho ya lo más difícil: levantar un 2-4, un 3-5 y un 4-5 y pelota de set. En esa situación se sacó una dejada de la chistera. Servía con 6-5 para cerrar la manga inicial. Lo que pasa es que las dudas al servicio del tenista de El Palmar las aprovechó Shapovalov para romper por tercera vez el saque de su rival y llevar el desenlace a la muerte súbita. La grada de la central del Ariake Coliseum no disimulaba sus colores. La muerte súbita fue un punto de inflexión en el partido. El campeón de siete grandes había tomado ventaja a pesar de los 29 puntos perdidos al saque. Con 1-0 en la continuación, al canadiense le tuvieron que atender en los vestuarios a la altura de la cadera. Denis, el 46 del ranking a sus 27 años, hace tiempo que no acostumbra a jugar duelos de tanta intensidad. Estuvo en pista dos juegos más antes de sacar la bandera blanca. Había transcurrido una hora y 22 minutos desde el inicio. Ya son 40 las victorias de Alcaraz contra zurdos por 12 derrotas. De los 14 jugadores que responden a ese perfil en el 'top100' no hay ninguno más con vida en Tokio. "Estoy lejos de donde quiero estar, pero estoy haciendo las cosas bien fuera de la pista porque estoy entrenando bien. Los próximos partidos y torneos los voy a utilizar para sentirme mejor", reflexionaba el número tres mundial. Otro zurdo, Ben Shelton, que acechaba al español en el ranking tras su final en el US Open, está hoy a 580 puntos. El estadounidense se borró de Tokio y falta ver si estará en condiciones de reaparecer en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái. La regularidad adquirida por Carlitos con el paso del tiempo se demuestra en la estadística. Son seis campañas seguidas con un mínimo de 30 partidos ganados a pesar de que en 2026 se perdió más de cuatro meses de competición por la muñeca.

articles.title: Horario y dónde ver la semifinal de Tokio entre Alcaraz y Munar
articles.standfirst: El murciano domina los precedentes entre ambos por tres victorias a una
articles.summary: El murciano domina los precedentes entre ambos por tres victorias a una
articles.body: El tenis masculino español tendrá este martes la posibilidad de lograr el sexto título de la presente temporada y el segundo en la gira asiática después del logrado el pasado martes por Alejandro Davidovich en Chengdu. El duelo fratricida de este lunes entre Carlos Alcaraz y Jaume Munar en las semifinales del Open 500 de Tokio garantiza la presencia de un miembro de la Armada en la última ronda. Además de Alcaraz, campeón la pasada edición, otros tres españoles jugaron por la corona en la capital japonesa: Manolo Orantes (1975 y 1977), David Ferrer (2007) y Rafael Nadal (2010-11). Los tres llegaron a levantar el trofeo. Carlitos y Munar han jugado cuatro veces en el circuito y el murciano domina los precedentes por tres triunfos a uno. La victoria del mallorquín llegó en el primer cara a cara entre ambos, en las semifinales de Marbella 2021. La primera semifinal de Tokio entre Carlos Alcaraz y Jaume Munar se celebrará este lunes, en la central del Ariake Coliseum, a partir de las 09.00 horas en España. El partido de semifinales del Open 500 de Tokio entre Carlos Alcaraz y Jaume Munar se podrá seguir en España a través de Movistar+, plataforma que tiene los derechos de la competición. Además habrá una amplia información del torneo en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Alcaraz se acuerda de Shapovalov en su firma a la cámara tras meterse en semifinales: "Regresa pronto Denis"
articles.standfirst: El murciano dejó un bonito detalle tras la lesión del canadiense y que le hizo abandonar
articles.summary: El murciano dejó un bonito detalle tras la lesión del canadiense y que le hizo abandonar
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz es el jugador más querido y admirado en los vestuarios del circuito profesional de tenis por detalles como el que dejó en los cuartos de Tokio. Tras pasa a las semifinales por la retirada de Denis Shapovalov a la conclusión del tercer juego del segundo set, el murciano no pasó por alto el problema físico que había obligado a decir adiós antes de tiempo al norteamericano. "Regresa pronto Denis", firmó en la cámara del torneo japonés. Otro gesto que le engrandece aún más. Hasta el momento del abandono Shapovalov había presentado una dura batalla al vigente campeón e incluso dispuso de una pelota de set, con 5-4. No es la primera vez que el joven de El Palmar tiene un gesto de estas características para sus compañeros de profesión. La pasada campaña, tras no poder continuar Jannik Sinner en la final del Masters 1000 de Cincinnati, le mandó un mensaje a través de la cámara: "Lo siento Jannik". El italiano se había sentido indispuesto.

Alcaraz y la firma dedicada a Sinner.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka suffers shock China Open exit, falls to Nikola Bartunkova in straight sets
articles.summary: World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka suffered a shock third-round exit at the China Open on Sunday, losing 6-4, 6-3 to Czech Republic’s Nikola Bartunkova.
articles.body: World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka suffered a shock third-round exit at the China Open on Sunday, losing 6-4, 6-3 to Czech Republic’s Nikola Bartunkova. The 34th-ranked Bartunkova produced one of the biggest upsets of the tournament, defeating the four-time Grand Slam champion in one hour and 34 minutes. The Czech hit four aces and capitalised on Sabalenka’s struggles to close out a straight-sets victory.Sabalenka had five break-point opportunities in the opening set but was unable to convert any of them. Bartunkova, meanwhile, stayed composed on the big points and secured the only break she needed to take the first set 6-4.The Czech continued to dictate the contest in the second set, breaking Sabalenka and maintaining her advantage to close out the match 6-3. The defeat continues Sabalenka’s difficult record at the Beijing tournament. The Belarusian has never progressed beyond the quarterfinals at the China Open.Top two seeds now outSabalenka arrived in Beijing looking to bounce back from her US Open disappointment, where she was denied a third consecutive title by Elena Rybakina. However, Rybakina herself suffered a surprise defeat earlier in Beijing, losing to unseeded Alina Charaeva in the second round.The early exits of the top two seeds mean neither Rybakina nor Sabalenka will feature in the latter stages of the WTA 1000 tournament. The China Open is being played on hard courts in Beijing from September 30 to October 11. Bartunkova will next face Austria’s Sinja Kraus, who defeated Ukraine’s Dayana Yastremska 6-1, 6-4.The Czech will now have an opportunity to extend her breakthrough run in Beijing after taking down one of the tournament’s biggest names.In the men’s draw, top seed Alexander Zverev is scheduled to face Novak Djokovic in the quarterfinals. articles.title: China Open: Aryna Sabalenka stunned by Nikola Bartunkova in Beijing
articles.summary: World number two Aryna Sabalenka follows Elena Rybakina out the door at the China Open as she falls to a surprise defeat by Nikola Bartunkova.
articles.body:
World number two Aryna Sabalenka followed Elena Rybakina out the door at the China Open as she fell to a surprise defeat by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova.

It comes a day after top seed Rybakina, who defeated Sabalenka in last month's US Open final and replaced the Belarusian at the top of the rankings, was knocked out by Armenian world number 118 Alina Charaeva.

Czech Bartunkova sprung another upset at the WTA 1000 tournament and continued her breakthrough season with a 6-4 6-3 over Sabalenka.

"I focused on myself, to be calm," said Bartunkova, who will face Austria's Sinja Kraus next.

"She's a legend, so I'm really happy that I won the match."

It is the first time since 2015 that the top two seeds have failed to reach the round of 16 at the China Open.

Sabalenka has not won a title since completing the 'Sunshine Double' in March, when she triumped at Indian Wells and the Miami Open back-to-back.

It has been a mixed year for Sabalenka by her high standards. She will finish without a Grand Slam trophy for the first time since 2022 and has often struggled to control her frustrations on court.

Against Bartunkova, she failed to convert any of her five break points and she threw her racquet after falling a break down early in the second set.

Kartal wins again as Zverev sets up Djokovic tie

At the Japan Open, Carlos Alcaraz reached the semi-finals after Denis Shapovalov retired with an injury to his right thigh.

Alcaraz, the defending champion in Tokyo, saved a set point in the opening set and was leading 7-6 (7-3) 2-1 when the Canadian was forced to withdraw.

It is just Alcaraz's third event since returning from a wrist injury at last month's US Open, where he fell to Ben Shelton in the quarter-finals.

He will face fellow Spaniard Jaume Munar for a place in the final.

articles.title: China Open: Aryna Sabalenka suffers shock Beijing exit — a day after new world No 1 Elena Rybakina was knocked out
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka exits the Beijing tournament in straight sets against Czech teenager Nikola Bartunkova, while Carlos Alcaraz advances in Tokyo; you can watch the WTA/ATP China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Czech 20-year-old Nikola Bartunkova defeated the four-time Grand Slam champion 6-4 6-3, leaving the tournament without its two top seeds in the opening week.

Rybakina was knocked out on Saturday, and Sabalenka has now joined her in an early exit from the WTA 1000 event in Beijing.

Sabalenka, who was denied a US Open three-peat by Rybakina last month, squandered five break points in the opening set as her struggles in Beijing continued.

The 28-year-old Belarusian has never progressed beyond the quarter-finals at the tournament.

Bartunkova, the No 26 seed, will next face Austria's 24-year-old Sinja Kraus, who defeated Dayana Yastremska 6-1 6-4 earlier on Sunday.

Fifth seed Mirra Andreeva eased into the fourth round with a 6-4 6-1 victory over Polina Kudermetova.

The French Open champion fired six aces and converted five of seven break-point opportunities to overwhelm her Uzbek opponent in just 68 minutes.

Top seed Carlos Alcaraz advanced to the semi-finals of the Japan Open after Denis Shapovalov was forced to retire with a hip injury, extending the Spaniard's strong return from a four-month wrist injury lay-off.

The defending champion was leading 7-6 (7-4) 2-1 when the Canadian called it a day.

"It was a little bit frustrating with my serve. I couldn't find a good way of serving: I was struggling almost every game on serve," Alcaraz said after dropping serve three times in the opening set.

"But I'm just happy with the way I came back after every break. It was a great first set: Great points, great rallies."

The Spaniard said he was disappointed to progress in such circumstances.

"It's a shame that he had to pull out. Going through to a semi-final like this is not the way I wanted, but sometimes sports are tough. You have to accept it. Hopefully he's going to be able to play in Shanghai healthy."

Alcaraz will face compatriot Jaume Munar in the semi-finals after the qualifier defeated France's Kyrian Jacquet 6-4 6-2.

articles.title: Sabalenka, Rybakina handed shock defeats at China Open tennis
articles.summary: The Belarusian’s exit follows top seed Rybakina losing to unseeded Charaeva in her first match as world number one.
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka was swatted aside in straight sets by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova in the third round of the China Open, leaving the event without its top two seeds as world number one Elena Rybakina was ousted in the second round.

Czech player Bartunkova, 20, sent down four aces to beat the former world number one 6-4, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes on Sunday.

“I focused on myself, to be calm,” Bartunkova said.

“She’s a legend … so I’m really happy that I won the match,” she said of the four-time Grand Slam champion.

Bartunkova next faces Austria’s Sinja Kraus in the round of 16.

Second-seeded Sabalenka squandered five chances to break serve in the sixth game of the first set, with Bartunkova strong on defence and firing deep.

The 28-year-old from Belarus threw on a cap for the eighth game of the first set as the women switched between playing in the shade and the sun, but it did not turn the tide in her favour.

A frustrated Sabalenka tossed her racquet at a break down in the fourth game of the second set, and lost on the first match point when she returned into the net.

Earlier on Saturday, Elena Rybakina – who replaced Sabalenka as the world number one last month – was ousted by Alina Charaeva in the second round.

Top seed Alexander Zverev was scheduled to play Novak Djokovic later on Sunday in the quarterfinals of the men’s 500-level event also taking place.

The 39-year-old Serbian great enters the match with an extraordinary unbeaten streak in Beijing, but Zverev — last month’s US Open champion — is in the running for the top men’s ranking.
